pencereler.0-5: An airliner suddenly pitched down and dove into the Pacific. The pilots fought it
pencereler.5-12: for minutes, but all eighty eight aboard died. The tail's trim was driven by a single jackscrew. Its nut
pencereler.12-20: needed regular grease. Maintenance intervals had been stretched again and again. The threads wore away until the nut could no longer hold.
pencereler.20-30: The tail slipped, and the jet became uncontrollable. Lubrication and wear checks were tightened across the fleet.

segmentler.metin: Alaska Airlines Flight 261 dove into the Pacific Ocean.
It took only a jackscrew nut worn out by too little lubrication.
So how could a jackscrew nut worn out by too little lubrication do this?
The answer is stripped acme nut threads on the horizontal stabilizer trim jackscrew — and it is why lubrication and end-play inspection intervals were tightened.
